title: Plan — through I2C
subtitle: Baseline tier UART → SPI → I2C. Left: the ordered work list. Right: why I2C is last of the three.

nodes.text:
Milestone 1 done
shared hardware layer signed off

1  UART RTL test fixed
TB edge latch + full 114-word load + JNZ tx_start
(done 2026-09-20: 4/4 bytes, cells 8.6-8.7 us)

2  regression + docs
TBs into run_all.sh, synth_area, glossary, 174 -> 173

3  commit milestone 2
CPU, SoC, assembler, emulator, firmware, TBs

4  pin matrix / OE
open-drain, read-back, tri-state (+ own TB)

5  I2C SoC wiring
pin matrix + 1 us tick (40 clocks)

6  I2C firmware
START/STOP, byte, ACK, repeated START, read

7  tb_pe_i2c_soc.v
checks timing, not just bits

DONE: real I2C transaction in firmware
on RTL, timing-checked, emulator parity
why I2C last of the baseline three?

UART: 2 pins, push-pull
no unbuilt hardware needed

SPI: 4 pins, push-pull
generated clock, still no OE

I2C: open-drain NEEDED
OE + read-back + arbitration

1 us tick = 40 clocks
tLOW 5, tHIGH 6 -> 90.9 kbit/s

read path budget
tLOW - tVD;DAT - tSU;DAT = 40 cycles

IMEM 114/128 today -> 1P_1024x16
(14% of die) when protocol 2 lands
